name: Aabenraa
title: Thickness Measurement Aabenraa | Bulk Carriers and Coasters
description: Ship thickness measurement at Aabenraa for bulk carriers, coasters and project cargo ships: hold, hatch-coaming, ballast tank and deck UTM, MPI checks.
h1: Hull and Hold Thickness Gauging for Bulk and Project Cargo Ships at Aabenraa
intro: Aabenraa lies at the head of a deep fjord on the east coast of Southern Jutland, and its port is built around dry bulk and project cargo rather than ferries or containers. Bulk carriers and coasters discharge and load grain, feed, fertiliser and other dry cargoes, and project ships handle heavy components over its quays. A cargo stay in the fjord is usually long enough for a focused gauging scope. Atlantis covers it with technicians who travel from India to the ship for that call.

highlights.p: Aabenraa Fjord gives ships a sheltered approach and calm water alongside, which suits gauging. Readings on hatch covers, coamings and open decks are less at the mercy of the weather here than at exposed North Sea or Skagerrak berths.

Grain, feed and fertiliser cargoes are discharged hold by hold. As each hold empties and is cleaned for access, the team can gauge frames, brackets, hopper and lower stool plating while the remaining holds are still being worked.

Fertiliser cargoes attack hold coatings and steel faster than grain, especially when moisture gets in. Owners of ships in that trade want hold frames and bulkhead plating measured more often than the class minimum, and a discharge call is a convenient time.

port.h: Aabenraa Fjord and its bulk port
p: Aabenraa Fjord cuts westwards into the coast of Southern Jutland from the southern Little Belt, and its deep, sheltered water has long made it a natural harbour. The town lies at the head of the fjord, with the commercial port along its shore, while the southern side of the fjord was for decades the site of the Ensted power station and its coal terminal, which received larger bulk carriers than most Danish ports could take. Ships reach the fjord from the Baltic through the waters between Funen and Als, passing some of the narrower channels of the Danish archipelago. There is no significant tide, and the fjord is sheltered from most wind directions, so berthing and cargo work are rarely interrupted by the weather.

Today the port is a dry-bulk and project cargo harbour. Grain and feed for the farms of Southern Jutland and northern Germany, fertiliser, aggregates, timber and other bulk commodities pass over its quays, and large storage areas serve heavy and project cargoes. Most ships calling are short-sea bulk carriers and coasters trading within the Baltic and North Sea, with larger handysize bulk carriers on some cargoes, alongside general cargo and project ships. The port is close to the German border and the motorway corridor into Germany, giving it a hinterland on both sides of the frontier. Unlike the Jutland ports on the Kattegat or the North Sea, Aabenraa has no ferry service, so its berths belong to cargo ships whose stays are counted in days rather than hours.

That pattern is useful for inspection. A bulk carrier discharging grain or fertiliser at Aabenraa may spend a day or more alongside, working hold by hold, and the crew is available to open ballast tanks and ventilate them while cargo operations continue. Project cargo ships stay for as long as loading heavy components takes, which can include waiting for weather, lifting plans or the cargo itself. Winters are mild by Baltic standards and the fjord seldom freezes, though ships that also load in the northern Baltic in winter carry ice-class notations and arrive with the wear that ice leaves on the shell. The harvest months bring a seasonal peak in grain and feed shipments, and with it more bulk calls.

facilities.h: Gauging at Aabenraa's quays and in the fjord
p: Almost all gauging at Aabenraa is done alongside during cargo operations. The bulk quays allow the team to work on deck, hatch covers and coamings from the moment the ship berths, and to move into each hold as it is discharged and made safe for entry. Ballast tanks, the double bottom and the topside and hopper tanks are opened by the crew, gas-free and ventilated, following a sequence we agree with the chief officer so that cargo stability and ballasting are not affected. The sheltered berths also mean that work on hatch covers and open decks is seldom lost to wind and spray.

Aabenraa is not a docking port for merchant ships, and owners whose ships are due for a docking survey take them to yards elsewhere in Denmark, Germany or Poland. Several such yards lie within a short passage of the fjord, and readings taken during an Aabenraa discharge give them a steel estimate before the ship arrives. Ships waiting for cargo or laid up for a period can sometimes be accommodated in the port or at anchor in the fjord, by arrangement with the harbour, and those periods allow longer condition surveys on an idle ship. We do not book that kind of stay ourselves; the owner and agent agree it with the port, and we fit the team's mobilisation to the dates.
list: Bulk quays — hatch cover, coaming and hold gauging on bulk carriers and coasters as each hold is discharged and cleaned.
Ballast and double-bottom tanks — opened and ventilated by the crew in sequence while cargo work continues, for tank gauging alongside.
Project cargo berths — deck, tank-top and lashing-point structure on project and heavy-lift ships before or after loading heavy units.
Lay-by and waiting berths — longer owner's condition and pre-purchase surveys on ships idle between cargoes.
Docking yards in Denmark, Germany or Poland — renewal-survey gauging continued at the yard, with the Aabenraa readings carried forward.

context.h: Rules and trade patterns behind gauging at Aabenraa
p: Denmark applies port state control through the Danish Maritime Authority under the Paris MoU, and bulk carriers attract close attention on structure: wasted hold frames, corroded hatch coamings, holed air pipes and leaking hatch covers are common deficiencies. Bulk carriers are also covered by the Enhanced Survey Programme, which ties close-up survey and thickness measurement to the ship's age and survey number, so a bulk carrier at fifteen or twenty years arriving in Aabenraa may be part-way through a demanding survey cycle. Under the EU ETS, which has applied to shipping since 2024, ships above the size threshold report emissions on their voyages to and from the port.

The cargoes themselves are part of the picture. Fertilisers and some other bulk commodities are hygroscopic or chemically aggressive and attack coatings and steel in holds when moisture is present, while grain is kinder to the structure but demands clean, sound holds. Ships alternating between these cargoes can show accelerated wastage on frames, brackets and lower bulkhead plating, and condensation on hold sides in Baltic winters adds to it. Charterers in the fertiliser trade may ask for evidence of hold condition, and an owner's gauging of holds during an Aabenraa call, with the areas of substantial corrosion mapped, answers that question directly.

jobs.h: The gauging work we see at Aabenraa
jobs.p: Aabenraa jobs are mostly bulk-carrier work fitted into cargo calls, scoped by the superintendent around the survey the ship is due for and the condition of its holds. Typical requests follow an annual survey at which the class surveyor recorded suspect areas, a charterer's question about hold condition before a fertiliser contract, or the run-up to an intermediate or renewal survey where the owner wants to know the steel quantity in advance. Project cargo ships bring a smaller number of jobs, usually on decks and tank tops that carry concentrated loads. We report to the superintendent each day so that decisions can be taken before the ship sails.
list: A handysize bulk carrier discharging grain: hold frames, brackets and lower stool plating gauged as each hold is emptied, before its intermediate survey.
A coaster in the fertiliser trade: owner's condition gauging of hold sides and transverse bulkheads, with pitting depths recorded.
Hatch cover and coaming gauging, with crack detection at cleats and coaming stays, after a class recommendation on weathertightness.
Pre-docking estimate on topside, hopper and double-bottom tanks for a bulk carrier heading to a Baltic yard for its renewal survey.
Deck and tank-top checks on a project cargo ship before loading heavy units, for an owner confirming the strengthened areas.

logistics: Billund Airport and Hamburg Airport are both within reach by road, and Copenhagen is an alternative with onward rail connections into Southern Jutland. Denmark's membership of the Schengen area means the team travels from India on Schengen visas, which must be arranged in advance. The ship's agent arranges port access, and because Aabenraa stays depend on cargo readiness, we confirm travel once the berthing date is firm.

faqs.q: Can holds be gauged while a ship discharges at Aabenraa?
faqs.a: Yes, one hold at a time. Once a hold is empty, swept and made safe for entry, the team can gauge frames, brackets, side plating, hopper and stool areas, using the ship's lighting and access arrangements. Holds still under discharge are left until they are clear, so the sequence follows the stevedores' plan, and the most important holds are agreed with the superintendent beforehand.

faqs.q: How much can be gauged during one cargo call?
faqs.a: It depends on the length of the call and how many crew are free to open and ventilate tanks. On a typical discharge, deck, hatch covers, coamings and the emptied holds can usually be covered, with a selection of ballast tanks if the crew can prepare them in sequence. Larger renewal-survey scopes may need a second call or the docking itself, and we say so when the plan is agreed.

faqs.q: Do fertiliser cargoes change what should be gauged?
faqs.a: They change where to look first. Fertiliser and similar cargoes attack coatings and steel in holds when damp, so hold frames, brackets, the lower parts of transverse bulkheads and the tank top deserve closer gauging, with pitting recorded by depth and extent. If the ship alternates between fertiliser and grain, the owner also needs evidence that holds remain fit for the cleaner cargo.

faqs.q: Where do ships calling at Aabenraa go for dry-docking?
faqs.a: To yards chosen by the owner, often elsewhere in Denmark, in northern Germany or in Poland, all within a short passage of the fjord. Each reading taken at Aabenraa is tied to the TM plan's frames and strakes, which lets the docking yard plan steel renewal and the class surveyor review condition before the ship arrives. Our technicians can also travel on to the yard.
